title: TCS Launches Biggest Leadership Overhaul in Three Years to Counter AI Disruption
excerpt: India's largest IT services company has reshuffled a dozen senior executives, split its banking division, and created five new business units after posting its first annual revenue decline since going public.
body:
• Tata Consultancy Services has reassigned about a dozen senior executives across service lines, industry groups, and country operations in its most sweeping leadership reshuffle since 2024.
  • The company's banking unit in North America, which generates a third of overall revenue, has been split into West Coast and East Coast divisions under new leadership.
  • TCS created five new business groups — ServiceNow, Travel and Transport, Energy and Utilities, US West Coast, and Autonomous Business Operations — expanding its business segments from seven to nine.
  • The restructuring follows TCS's first full-year revenue decline since its 2004 listing and a 16% churn rate among senior executives, with 300 of 1,800 senior leaders departing by March 2026.

Tata Consultancy Services has launched its most aggressive organizational restructuring in three years, reshuffling about a dozen senior executives and creating five new business units as India's largest IT services company scrambles to adapt to AI-driven disruption that threatens the $315 billion outsourcing industry.

Splitting the Core

The most significant structural change targets TCS's biggest revenue engine. The banking, financial services, and insurance (BFSI) Americas unit — which accounts for roughly a third of the company's $30 billion in annual revenue — has been split into two divisions. Company veterans Rakesh Kumar and Mohan Veeturi will lead the West Coast and East Coast banking units respectively, according to internal memos from CEO K. Krithivasan and COO Aarthi Subramanian seen by Reuters.

Susheel Vasudevan, who previously oversaw the combined BFSI Americas business for nearly three years, has been elevated to lead TCS's 50 largest clients, each generating more than $100 million in annual revenue. The move effectively creates a concentrated strategic accounts layer designed to deepen wallet share with marquee customers, according to Mint.

"We believe this will help in deepening customer centricity, which is pivotal to our growth."

— TCS internal statement on the restructuring

Five New Business Groups

TCS has carved out five new verticals, expanding its business segments from seven to nine. The new groups include a ServiceNow practice led by Rajnish Palande, a Travel, Transport and Hospitality unit under Arun Pradeep Surendra Mohan, an Energy, Resources and Utilities division headed by Sabyasachi Chandra, a US West Coast Business Group under Akhilesh Tripathi, and an Autonomous Business Operations unit led by Akhilesh Tiwari.

The Autonomous Business Operations group is positioned as one of the more forward-looking bets. "Autonomous Business Operations is emerging as a significant opportunity for TCS as clients look to reimagine business processes, improve productivity, build resilience, and unlock AI-led operating models," COO Subramanian wrote in an internal email seen by The Hindu BusinessLine.

The US West Coast unit has been set up to focus on what TCS describes as "the world's most important innovation hubs," with a mandate to bring together technology companies, startups, and academia.

The life sciences and healthcare business ($3.1 billion in FY26 revenue) and the energy, resources and utilities business ($1.8 billion) were carved out from a previously combined unit. The cybersecurity vertical also received new leadership after a year in which several high-profile TCS clients — including Marks & Spencer, Co-op, and Jaguar Land Rover — were hit by cyberattacks.

Behind the Shake-Up

The restructuring comes at a critical juncture for TCS. The company posted $30.02 billion in revenue for FY26, a 0.5% decline that marked its first full-year revenue drop since going public in August 2004. The rise of AI has stoked fears about the future of the outsourcing model, with clients increasingly seeking shorter project timelines, productivity gains, and lower prices.

Senior management turnover has added urgency. At least 300 of 1,800 senior executives — including principal consultants, vice presidents, and senior vice presidents with over two decades of experience — had quit by March 2026, representing a 16% churn rate, according to Mint. TCS also laid off over 12,000 employees in the same period.

"Energy offers recurring revenue, travel is seeing strong momentum, and cybersecurity is emerging as an increasingly important horizontal. It is logical to carve these into standalone units."

— Sushovon Nayak, Lead IT Analyst, Anand Rathi Institutional Equities

Context and Outlook

The reorganization was communicated to business unit heads by Krithivasan and Subramanian on a Friday evening, immediately after the management spent the first half of the day discussing first-quarter earnings. TCS beat quarterly revenue estimates for the April-June period, helped by higher spending by banking clients and weakness in the rupee.

Since COO Subramanian took on expanded responsibilities in April 2025, TCS has tightened its operating cadence, with the CEO and COO conducting regular weekend reviews with business unit heads. Industry analysts see the latest moves as an attempt to pivot toward higher-value, AI-augmented services while protecting margins and sharpening focus on strategic accounts.

For investors and the broader Indian IT services sector, TCS's restructuring is a bellwether. If India's largest outsourcer is reorganizing at this scale to meet the AI moment, smaller competitors face the same pressures with fewer resources to respond.
